description:
📣 **A SPEC GAINS DEFENSIBILITY THROUGH ADOPTION, NOT THROUGH CLAUSES — and koine has never been implemented by anyone outside this tree.** The 2026-08-13 portfolio scan put koine at 7/10 with the highest headroom of any project in the portfolio, and the lever is not more specification. koine is already ~60% profiles-over-standards and its recent direction is explicitly to ADOPT rather than restate (`73`, `74`, `77`, `78` all merged). Adding clauses now moves the score down, not up.

**What would move it is evidence that the contract works between parties who do not share a codebase.** Today every implementation of KINP/KGP/KCB/KMI/KFT is in this tree — agora, cuneiform's exports, lugh — all authored by one operator. A contract exercised only by its author is a format, not a standard, and that is the honest reading of the 7.

**Two things make this the right moment.** First, `79-conformance-gated-ratification` merged: koine adopted MCP's SEP-2484 pattern, *a spec cannot reach Final without a matching conformance suite*, so the machinery to prove a third-party implementation conforms already exists. Second, [Kang & Diponegoro (arXiv 2606.31498, 30 June 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31498) independently concluded that agent-community governance is *"a missing architectural layer above current interoperability standards, not a missing feature within them"* — koine's own thesis, reached by people who had never seen it. **That is external demand evidence, and it is the strongest asset koine has for attracting an implementer.**

**Be honest about what this is.** This is partly a positioning and outreach tasklist rather than an engineering one, which is unusual for this tree and should not be disguised. It is also **not** open-sourcing koine — that is a separate, company-level decision (`ADR-0007`-class) and nothing here presumes it.

userStories.title: Make the contract implementable by someone who has not read the tree
userStories.description: Before asking for an implementer, check that the specs are sufficient without the surrounding context an insider carries.
acceptanceCriteria: Each spec is audited for **implicit dependence on this tree** — a clause only satisfiable by reading agora's source, a term defined nowhere, an example that assumes cuneiform's shapes. Every finding is either fixed or recorded as a known gap.
The audit is done against the ACTUAL artefacts a third party would receive — the specs, the JSON schemas, the relation registry, the conformance suite — and not against the repo as a whole.

The single hardest question is answered explicitly: **could a competent engineer implement KINP resolution and a KGP GroundingPack producer from the specs alone?** If not, name what is missing. `80`'s schema and registry gates are the mechanical half of this; this story is the semantic half.

userStories.title: One end-to-end run between two implementations that do not share code
userStories.description: The evidence that matters. Everything else is a claim about the specs; this is a measurement of them.
acceptanceCriteria: A KGP pack or a KCB capability produced by an implementation OUTSIDE this tree is consumed by one inside it, or the reverse, and the exchange is recorded with what worked and what did not.
It is run through the `79` conformance suite, so the result is a CONFORMANCE VERDICT rather than an anecdote — this is exactly what that machinery was adopted for.

Where the outside implementation had to guess, that guess is a finding against the spec. An interop exercise whose only output is 'it worked' has measured nothing; the value is in the ambiguities it surfaces.

If no external implementer can be found, the story is honestly re-scoped to the strongest available proxy — a clean-room implementation from the specs alone, by someone with no access to this tree's source — and the weaker evidential value is stated rather than glossed.

userStories.title: Publish the layer claim where the demand evidence already exists
userStories.description: The governance-gaps paper establishes the layer is missing. koine can cite it; it can also answer it.
acceptanceCriteria: A short public artefact states what koine specifies and, precisely, what it does NOT — the six governance dimensions of the paper that koine deliberately leaves alone (per `81`) belong in it, because a spec that says what it is not for is easier to adopt than one that appears to claim everything.
It cites the paper as independent evidence for the layer, and is honest that koine is pre-adoption: one operator, one tree, no external implementers yet.
Nothing commercially sensitive crosses over. `rosetta/strategy/` is ⛔ PRIVATE and names which projects become companies; this artefact draws only on koine's own public-facing material.
A DECLINE is acceptable and must be recorded if publishing conflicts with the open-source posture — that call is `ADR-0007`-class and is not taken here.
